WHAT MAKES US A GREAT PLACE TO WORK

We are proud to be consistently recognized as one of the world's best places to work. We are currently the top ranked consulting firm on Glassdoor's Best Places to Work list and have earned the #1 overall spot a record seven times. Extraordinary teams are at the heart of our business strategy, but these don't happen by chance. They require intentional focus on bringing together a broad set of backgrounds, cultures, experiences, perspectives, and skills in a supportive and inclusive work environment. We hire people with exceptional talent and create an environment in which every individual can thrive professionally and personally.

WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

Tech Insights Group (TIG) at Bain & Company is a rapidly growing global team of world-class consultants and technologists. We work with leading Private Equity (PE) investors and their tech-enabled portfolio companies to act as technical advisors in investment processes. We conduct product and technology due diligence engagements and value creation assignments, leveraging our extensive expertise in software and understanding of commercial environments specific to tech-enabled businesses. We deliver our projects by combining a team of consultants with CPOs and CTOs of leading global technology and software companies with decades of both advising and operating experience. The team has completed 400+ product and technology diligences and value creation engagements worldwide. Over the past 4 years, we supported our clients on some of the most visible technology investments in the US and Europe, including several of the Top 2024 and Top 2025 software deals. We conduct engagements spanning enterprise applications, vertical applications (HCIT, FinTech, EdTech), infrastructure software, cloud software, and tech enabled services (IT services, e-Commerce, AdTech). We also help funds understand GenAI disruption potential and opportunities to inform their investment thesis. Bain's Tech Insights practice is a place where agile minds work powerfully and nimbly together, thriving on spirited discussion. The Tech Insights Group operates within the Expert Client Delivery (ECD) team, a global capability area designed to provide support to clients across Europe and beyond through a single, globally organized team. TIG enhances our Private Equity Group (PEG) and General Consulting (GC) capabilities by offering specialized technical expertise to support our clients at every stage of the investment lifecycle from deal generation and due diligence to portfolio value creation and exit planning.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Joining Technology Insights Group (TIG) is an exciting opportunity to build a new and critical capability at Bain. You will work closely with the global Tech leadership and the regional private equity (PE) teams.

At Bain, you will leverage your technology and consulting experience in actively contributing to projects, assessing key aspects of leading software companies for PE investors. You will help our clients strategically approach how technology will shape their businesses and solve some of the most challenging issues they face. Additionally, you will gain direct exposure to CEOs, Executives, and Private Equity professionals.

This is a particularly exciting time to join the team - we have ambitious growth plans and you will be contributing to scaling a growing global capability within Bain & Company.

Responsibilities in Detail:

Lead and drive technology due diligence and value creation assignments on behalf of PE investors targeting software businesses.
Actively contribute across the entire client engagement, from formulating the project scope to building and presenting the final report.
Drive and support the primary and secondary research efforts of the team; collect and analyze quantitative and qualitative data across a variety of sources.
Conduct hypothesis-led problem solving, communicate complex ideas, and approach problems strategically.
Effectively develop and communicate recommendations and insights to the project team, PE investors, and technology leaders.
Help to build and scale a new business, act as thought partner to Tech leadership on our growth and strategy.
Enhance Bain's Tech Insights Groups brand through external reputation building and marketing efforts.
Invest in special initiatives and projects that help us scale the practice (ops/systems)

ABOUT YOU

Open to current MBA students who are graduating this winter/recently graduated, and are available to start this Spring of 2027.

The Consultant, Technology Insights Group role requires passion for transformation, an entrepreneurial spirit, empathy, and technical aptitude.

The following are highly valued:

Passion for software

Demonstrate a passion for software as well as the tech industry more broadly (e.g., digital transformation, disruptive business models).
3+ years in a software or technology related position or industry; Technical diligence experience preferred.
Ability to rapidly absorb and interpret technical information.
Inquisitive mindset and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment.

Client service orientation and EQ

Passion for delivering high-impact client results in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Exceptional interpersonal skills and emotional agility, ability to interface across any level at Bain and client organizations.
Outstanding oral and written communication skills.

Entrepreneurial mindset and teamwork

Desire to join a rapidly growing startup within a leading strategy consulting firm
Entrepreneurial, curious, creative, and innovative thinking.
Strong alignment with Bain operating principles.
Strong teamwork ethos and ability to work with team members with diverse skills and backgrounds in an inclusive fashion.

Management potential

Demonstrated potential for developing and coaching junior team members.
Direct management experience in a consulting or operating line preferred.

Strong analytical capabilities and background

Analytical and data-driven mindset.
Aptitude for creative, quantitative, and qualitative problem solving.
Undergraduate/Master's degree from a top tier university in a relevant field (i.e., computer science, engineering, business management, information systems).
MBA and Top tier consulting experience preferred.

YOUR CAREER

Throughout your career at Bain you will participate in world class formal and informal training programmes in order to ensure you continuously develop your skills. In addition, you will be assigned a mentor to help guide you through your career and will develop a network of your peers across teams and offices. Working alongside an outstanding group of individuals, you will develop and enhance your own technology expertise, commercial acumen, and analytical capabilities. Whether your long-term goal is to grow with us, join a PE/VC firm, work in the tech/software industry, or to start the next great technology company, you will build a fantastic foundation by joining our multi-talented and highly motivated team.

notes:
Tailored for Bain TIG (technology due diligence and value creation for PE investors in software). The spine is the consulting arc plus a software-operator record, in that order: Valeo diagnosis -> sized recommendation is hypothesis-led problem solving with a number on it, and everything under it is the "3+ years in a software or technology position" the JD asks for.

Against the offline ranking: pinned nutanix-sales-acv (scored 4) and nutanix-files-migration (3). The scorer buries them because this JD never says revenue or ACV, but a PE tech-diligence reader is scanning for exactly those - $40-50M ACV and $1M+ recurring revenue off enterprise customers are the two numbers that prove he has lived inside a software P&L. Same for nutanix-team-budget (6): "direct management experience in a consulting or operating line preferred" is a stated criterion and 11+ engineers on a $500K budget answers it directly.

Demoted iitj-ignus (scored 1) out and kept iitj-mentoring in against the master ordering: the JD names "developing and coaching junior team members" as a criterion, and people-forward ("Coached junior students one-to-one") mirrors that wording. Excluded amantya-ios-retail (2016-2018 already thin; Amantya drops off the page entirely). Excluded touchnote-new-revenue to pay for the page - it cost 2 lines and touchnote-checkout is the stronger Touchnote bullet here, since conversion / AOV / cart abandonment are the unit-economics vocabulary of a commercial diligence and e-Commerce is a named TIG sector. Kept nutanix-code-standards (quality-forward) despite it being the weakest Nutanix bullet: code quality, defect rates and engineering standards are literally what a product-and-technology diligence assesses, so it earns its line for this JD specifically. It is paid for by the Technologies line, trimmed to one line by dropping Containerisation (implied by Kubernetes) and Scripting - that buys a whole bullet for two keywords, and the trim deliberately keeps Enterprise, Infrastructure and Cloud Software, which are the JD s own sector words.

Variants chosen to mirror the JD: nutanix-sales-acv customer-forward (avoids repeating "product strategy", which everhaus-compliance owns on this page), nutanix-files-migration customer-forward (leads with enterprise customers and recurring revenue rather than the build), nutanix-team-budget people-forward ("Led and developed" answers "developing and coaching"), eleven01-mvp zero-to-one (the JD asks for someone who wants to "build and scale a new business" and "join a rapidly growing startup within a leading strategy consulting firm" - founding-member zero-to-one is the closest thing he has to that).

AI: both Valeo bullets on cursor-forward and valeo-route-app on ai-forward, same reasoning as the consulting archetype - the JD says TIG helps funds understand GenAI disruption, so naming Claude and Cursor is a checkable fact rather than a buzzword. overrideText on eleven01-mvp is a pure reword ("product roadmap" -> "the product direction") to clear the one repeated-phrase finding against everhaus-roadmap; no new claim.

Skills and Technologies lead with the JD s own words. Deliberately does NOT claim technology due diligence as a skill - he has never run one, and that is the headline gap to raise in the cover letter rather than a line to write on the CV.

2026-09-04, second pass after Parag supplied three new facts (all three are now points in the pool):
- nutanix-move-diligence: a real technical due diligence of the Move product - 400+ critical security and 500+ licence risks found, cut to 20 and zero with Legal and Compliance. This closes what had been the headline gap. It now LEADS the Nutanix block and is why the Skills line can honestly say "Technology Due Diligence" - before this it could not, and deliberately did not.
- valeo-cost-buyin: he presented the strategies to the CEO and operations leadership and won approval. Slotted straight after valeo-cost-strategy so Valeo now reads diagnose -> recommend -> sell it at C-level, which is the whole consulting arc in three lines. Paid for by moving valeo-cost-strategy to the short variant, which costs the "in Cursor with Claude" clause - a trade worth making, since Claude and Cursor still appear in the Technologies line and valeo-cost-diagnosis still names Cursor.
- nutanix-vp-roadmap is in the pool but OFF this page: it collides with nutanix-sales-acv (same roadmap-to-ACV argument) and valeo-cost-buyin already proves executive communication. Swap it in for nutanix-sales-acv only if a JD weights the presentation over the number.
Dropped nutanix-ai-workflow and nutanix-code-standards to pay for the diligence bullet. code-standards is straightforwardly superseded by move-diligence on the engineering-quality axis. ai-workflow goes because everhaus-operating-model already carries an AI-efficiency story and points.json records the two as colliding - keeping exactly one is the right call. Page still fits at scale 1 with zero overflow, still 16 bullets, overlap audit clean. 2026-09-04, third pass: Parag capped Valeo and EverHaus at two points each (internship and part-time work should not outweigh the full-time roles) and the freed lines went to nutanix-code-standards, eleven01-ico and iitj-ignus. Valeo keeping only two points forced a choice between the 30% recommendation and the CEO approval, so valeo-cost-buyin carries an overrideText merging both - both facts are his and valeo-cost-strategy is off this page, so nothing is double-counted; revisit if he would rather run the two points separately. Diligence bullet reworded on his instruction and promoted to the point default.
